name: Tunnel, greenhouse and vegetable farming

problems.words: Cucumber price crashed the week our whole tunnel came on at once
quick_ideas: Put every tunnel's planting date and expected picking window on one chart, so overlapping weeks show up early
Line up one non-mandi buyer before your next peak; crop and timing choices are for your agronomist.

workzap_build.text: A tunnel register and planting calendar that warns you automatically when several tunnels are due to peak in the same week.

problems.ask_first: How are planting dates decided at the moment?
problems.free_stops: How the calendar and warnings are set up for your tunnels goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk each tunnel and note which rows are picking heavily this week, so you see how much volume is hitting buyers together.
Give one person the weekly picking outlook in one notebook, so buyer calls happen before the rush reaches the packing area.

problems.words: I don't know what each tunnel earns after costs
quick_ideas: Number every tunnel and write the number beside each expense, so costs can be split later
Record harvest by tunnel for one cycle.

workzap_build.text: A tunnel register logging costs and harvest against each tunnel daily, with a profit view per tunnel per cycle.

problems.ask_first: How many tunnels or greenhouses do you run?
problems.free_stops: The cost heads and profit view design are part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: For one picking day, note each tunnel’s filled crates beside its worker hours, so low-output tunnels stop hiding behind busy ones.
Give one staff role one notebook for tunnel harvest and work notes after picking, so each tunnel’s performance can be reviewed later.

problems.words: Supermarket rejects part of every delivery and deducts it later
quick_ideas: Ask the driver to get rejections signed at the door with a photo, so deductions can be checked
Compare this month's deduction notes against those door records.

workzap_build.text: A delivery sheet per buyer recording rejections at the door with photos and matching them against later deductions, every delivery.

problems.ask_first: Do you get any written rejection note at delivery today?
problems.free_stops: How door records and deductions are matched goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Sort deduction notes by rejection reason from the last few deliveries, so the biggest cause of lost value is clear.
Give one packhouse role the job of keeping all delivery notes and deduction slips together, so disputes can be checked quickly.

problems.words: Hotel orders come on WhatsApp at midnight and we miss some
quick_ideas: Keep one number only for buyer orders, so they don't mix with other chats
Have one person turn messages into a morning list and confirm each buyer.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp order intake that turns hotel and restaurant messages into a confirmed order list every morning.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many hotel and restaurant buyers do you supply?
problems.free_stops: How messages become a confirmed list is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many buyer messages arrived after closing across one week, so you see the true size of the midnight order pile.
Give one role the job of writing all overnight orders onto one morning sheet, so kitchen buyers are not missed at dispatch.

problems.words: Invoices to restaurants go unpaid for months
quick_ideas: List every unpaid invoice by buyer and date, so you know who to chase first
Agree payment terms in writing with new buyers before the first delivery.

workzap_build.text: A buyer ledger for supermarkets and HORECA that ages every invoice and sends polite reminders when payments fall due.

problems.ask_first: Who are your slowest payers, supermarkets or restaurants?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and ledger setup are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each buyer’s unpaid papers with this week’s delivery notes, so regular late payers stand out before more produce goes out.
Give one office role one fixed weekly time to update all unpaid invoice notes, so follow-up keeps moving during harvest pressure.

problems.words: Harvested quantity and dispatched quantity never match
quick_ideas: Record harvest at the packing area and loads at the vehicle separately for a week, to see where the gap opens
Write down rejects and waste so the gap has an explanation.

workzap_build.text: Daily harvest entry by WhatsApp per tunnel with grade split, matched against dispatch every day.

problems.free_stops: How harvest and dispatch are matched is part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare packed crates, loaded crates and return crates for one dispatch day, so the handover point causing the mismatch shows.
Give one role the job of writing counts at packing and loading on the same sheet, so losses stop being argued about later.

problems.words: Pump or drip failure noticed only after the plants suffer
quick_ideas: Add a morning look at pumps and lines to one worker's day, so failures are caught early
Keep a breakdown book noting what failed and how long the fix took.

workzap_build.text: A daily equipment check per tunnel with photos, and a maintenance log that shows repeat failures.

problems.ask_first: How do you find out about a failure today?
problems.free_stops: The checklist and log design go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note where water flow looked weak during today's walk round, so recurring trouble spots are seen before another surprise stoppage.
Give one worker one page for pump and line checks at the same morning time, so faults get noticed before harvest suffers.

problems.words: Workers don't follow the daily task list in each tunnel
quick_ideas: Put a short task list on each tunnel door, so everyone sees the same jobs
Review missed items with the team once this week.

workzap_build.text: A daily task checklist per tunnel with photo proof and supervisor sign-off, showing which tunnels slip.

problems.ask_first: Is there a supervisor on site every day?
problems.free_stops: How tasks, proof and sign-off are set up is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the tunnel task lists with what was actually finished by evening, so the jobs most often skipped stand out.
Give one supervisor one place to collect all completed tunnel lists each day, so missed work is spotted before the next shift.

problems.words: Electricity and cooling bills eat the margin in summer
quick_ideas: Note meter and generator hours once a week, so you can see which month and source costs most
Put fuel fills next to generator hours; technical settings belong with your specialist.

workzap_build.text: A utility and diesel log against pump and generator hours with monthly cost per unit produced.

problems.ask_first: Which cost worries you most: power, water or diesel?
problems.free_stops: How readings are captured and costs worked out is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note power meter readings and cooling run hours on the same weekday, so the heaviest summer usage periods are easier to spot.
Give one staff role one notebook for meter readings, generator hours and bill dates, so utility records stay together for review.

problems.words: Box subscribers cancel and I don't know why
quick_ideas: Ask everyone who cancels for the reason, so you learn what is going wrong
Offer a skip-a-week option before cancelling.

workzap_build.text: A subscription box system handling weekly orders and skips, with every cancellation reason captured.

problems.ask_first: How do subscribers order and pay now?
problems.free_stops: How skips, orders and reasons are handled is part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each cancellation beside the last box contents and delivery day, so the main reason for drop-offs stands out.
Give one person a single notebook for pauses, complaints and cancellations, so follow-up stops getting missed after busy harvest days.

never_say: Anything on pesticides, fungicides, fertilisers, nutrient solutions, doses, pre-harvest intervals, climate settings or disease identification; refer to an agronomist or extension service.
What to grow for profit, or any price prediction.
Advice on food-safety, GAP or organic certification rules.
Any help relabelling produce as organic or local, or changing harvest dates on labels.
Visa or permit advice for seasonal workers; names or numbers of workers or buyers.

sample_reply.person: I've got 12 tunnels near Sheikhupura. What can I actually do so the cucumbers don't all hit the mandi in the same week?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be managed, and you can make a start this week. 1) Put every tunnel's planting date and expected picking window on one chart, so clashing weeks show up early. 2) Line up one hotel, restaurant or shop buyer before your next peak, and agree crop and timing choices with your agronomist. Workzap can do this automatically for you, with a tunnel calendar that warns you when several tunnels are due to peak together and logs harvest and costs per tunnel every day. Shall I get a solution document and quote prepared for you? You can say no.
